tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest


PROJECT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FIXTURE = PROJECT / "tests" / "fixtures" / "messages.csv"


class ReportTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_cli_writes_expected_counts(self):
        """The CLI saves a report for the intended input with counts 3 / 2 / 1."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="spam-lab-test-") as directory:
            output = Path(directory) / "summary.json"
            result = subprocess.run(

                cwd=PROJECT,

            self.assertTrue(output.is_file(), "The program did not save a report.")
            report = json.loads(output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(report["input_file"], str(FIXTURE))
            self.assertEqual(report["total_messages"], 3)

if __name__ == "__main__":

content.text:
Sprawdziłem środowisko i jest gotowe: niczego nie trzeba było instalować. Samego skryptu ani testu jeszcze nie uruchomiłem.

## Jak działa `describe_data.py`

Skrypt tylko liczy etykiety, które już są w danych. Nie trenuje modelu i nie uruchamia filtra SpamAssassin.

**Wejście:** `--data`, czyli plik CSV z kolumnami `message_id,text,label`. Jeden rekord to jeden e-mail. Pole `text` (temat i treść) zajmuje zwykle wiele linii fizycznych, dlatego plik jest czytany parserem CSV, a nie linia po linii ([describe_data.py:15](describe_data.py:15)).

**Sprawdzanie danych** w funkcji `describe` ([describe_data.py:13-32](describe_data.py:13)):
- nagłówki muszą mieć dokładnie postać `message_id, text, label`;
- żadne pole nie może być puste ani nadmiarowe;
- `message_id` nie może się powtarzać;
- `label` musi mieć wartość `ham` (zwykła poczta) albo `spam` (niechciana poczta);
- plik nie może być pusty.

Każdy błąd przerywa program komunikatem `Error: ...` i kodem wyjścia 1 ([describe_data.py:61-62](describe_data.py:61)).

**Wyjście:** `--out`, czyli raport JSON. Skrypt sam tworzy brakujący katalog i nadpisuje istniejący plik. Nie pozwala też zapisać raportu w miejsce pliku wejściowego ([describe_data.py:52](describe_data.py:52)). Pola raportu:
- `input_file`: bezwzględna ścieżka do pliku wejściowego.
- `input_sha256`: suma kontrolna bajtów wejścia. Pozwala porównać wersje pliku, ale nie mówi, czy dane są poprawne.
- `total_messages` i `label_counts`: liczba rekordów oraz liczby etykiet `ham` i `spam`.
- `runtime`: użyty interpreter, jego wersja i katalog roboczy.

Na koniec skrypt wypisuje w konsoli ścieżkę raportu i liczby etykiet.

**Test** [tests/test_report.py](tests/test_report.py) uruchamia skrypt na 3 sztucznych wiadomościach z [tests/fixtures/messages.csv](tests/fixtures/messages.csv). Raport zapisuje w katalogu tymczasowym. Sprawdza, że:
- kod wyjścia to 0;
- raport powstał;
- `input_file` wskazuje na ten plik testowy;
- wynik to 3 wiadomości: 2 `ham` i 1 `spam`.

Nie dotyka pliku `results/exercise-summary.json`.

## Środowisko

| Co sprawdziłem | Wynik |
|---|---|
| Katalog roboczy | `/Users/michal/studia/3 sem/mio - lab/lab1/project` |
| Python | `python3 --version` → **Python 3.14.5**, `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`. README wymaga wersji ≥ 3.10. |
| Gdzie działa | Lokalnie na Twoim MacBooku (macOS 26.5.1, arm64), nie w chmurze. |
| Zależności | Tylko biblioteka standardowa, więc bez `pip` i bez virtualenv. |
| Pliki | `data/exercise.csv`, `data/demo.csv`, test i plik testowy CSV są na miejscu. W `data/raw/` jest 12 plików. |
| `results/` | Katalogu jeszcze nie ma. Skrypt utworzy go przy pierwszym uruchomieniu, więc nie ma starego raportu, który można by wziąć za nowy. |

Szybko przeliczyłem rekordy osobnym poleceniem, więc to nie jest wynik `describe_data.py`. Wyszło tak:
- `data/exercise.csv`: **8 rekordów** w 203 liniach fizycznych;
- `data/demo.csv`: 4 rekordy w 123 liniach;
- plik testowy: 3 rekordy w 10 liniach.

To pokazuje, że liczenie linii nie daje liczby wiadomości.

## Następne kroki z README

Uruchomienie skryptu:
```bash
python3 describe_data.py --data data/exercise.csv --out results/exercise-summary.json
```

Odczytanie raportu:
```bash
cat results/exercise-summary.json
```

Uruchomienie testu (sukces to `Ran 1 test`, `OK` i kod wyjścia 0):
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

exercise-004,"Subject: [ILUG] Re: Problems with RAID1 on cobalt raq3

On Mon, Aug 19, 2002 at 03:08:16PM +0100, John P. Looney mentioned:
>  This is likely because to get it to boot, like the cobalt, I'm actually
> passing root=/dev/hda5 to the kernel, not /dev/md0. 

 Just to solve this...the reason I was booting the box with
root=/dev/hda5, not /dev/md0 was because /dev/md0 wasn't booting - it
would barf with 'can't find init'.

 It turns out that this is because I was populating md0 with tar. Which
seems to have 'issues' with crosslinked files - for instance, it was
trying to make a hard link of glibc.so to hda - and failing. It was only
as I did it again with a friend present, that he spotted the errors, and
queried them. We noticed that the hard linked files just didn't exist on
the new rootfs.

 When we duplicated the filesystems with dump instead of tar, it worked
fine, I was able to tell lilo to use root=/dev/md0 and everything worked.

 Woohoo.

Kate

wyjasnij mi do czego sluzy @data/manifest.json w tym projekcie?

`data/manifest.json` to dokumentacja pochodzenia danych. Opisuje, skąd wzięto wiadomości i jak sprawdzić, że pliki w projekcie się nie zmieniły. `describe_data.py` ani test w ogóle go nie czytają, więc dla programu jest to plik pomocniczy.

## Co zawiera

**1. Źródło zbioru (`dataset`, `prepared_on`, `sources`)**
- Dane pochodzą z publicznego korpusu Apache SpamAssassin. Zestaw przygotowano 22.10.2026.
- `sources` wskazuje dwa oryginalne archiwa: `easy_ham` (zwykła poczta) i `spam`. Dla każdego jest adres URL i suma SHA-256 archiwum.

**2. Sumy kontrolne paczek CSV (`packets`)**
- Każdy plik CSV (`demo.csv`, `exercise.csv`) ma swoją sumę SHA-256.
- Suma dla `exercise.csv` (`95e9049f…ed07`) jest taka sama jak `input_sha256` w Twoim raporcie [results/exercise-summary.json](results/exercise-summary.json). Raport powstał więc dokładnie z tej wersji danych, którą przygotowano w manifeście.

**3. Pochodzenie każdej wiadomości (`messages`)**

Każdy rekord łączy `message_id` z CSV z oryginałem:

| Pole | Znaczenie |
|---|---|
| `message_id` | identyfikator, np. `exercise-002`, taki sam jak w CSV |
| `packet` | plik CSV, w którym jest ta wiadomość |
| `label` | etykieta `ham` lub `spam` |
| `source` | archiwum źródłowe: `easy_ham` albo `spam` |
| `archive_member` | dokładna ścieżka pliku w oryginalnym archiwum |
| `raw_file` | lokalna kopia oryginału, np. `data/raw/exercise-002.eml` |
| `sha256` | suma kontrolna tego pliku `.eml` |

## Do czego się to przydaje

- **Śledzenie pochodzenia.** Dowolny rekord z CSV da się odnaleźć w `data/raw/` i w oryginalnym archiwum SpamAssassin.
- **Sprawdzanie integralności.** Porównując sumy, wykryjesz, czy CSV albo plik `.eml` zmieniono od przygotowania danych. Zgodna suma oznacza tylko, że plik jest ten sam. Nie znaczy, że etykiety są poprawne.
- **Wyjaśnienie etykiet.** Etykieta wynika z archiwum źródłowego: wiadomości z `easy_ham` mają `ham`, a z `spam` mają `spam`. W `exercise.csv` daje to 5 ham i 3 spam, tak samo jak w raporcie.
- **Powtarzalność.** Ktoś inny może pobrać te same archiwa i odtworzyć dokładnie ten zestaw.

Więcej o polach i przygotowaniu danych jest w [data/README.md](data/README.md).

content.text:
Tak, ale z kilkoma zastrzeżeniami.

**Co się zgadza:**
- SHA-256 zmienia się przy zmianie choćby jednego bajtu. Dotyczy to też zmienionej etykiety, usuniętego rekordu czy dopisanej spacji.
- Wystarczy więc przeliczyć sumę i porównać ją z manifestem, na przykład tak:

  ```bash
  shasum -a 256 data/exercise.csv data/demo.csv
  ```

  Dzięki osobnym sumom dla każdego pliku `.eml` widać też, która wiadomość się zmieniła.

**Zastrzeżenia:**
1. **Nikt nie sprawdza tego automatycznie.** `describe_data.py` tylko wpisuje sumę do raportu i nie porównuje jej z manifestem. Zmiana zostanie wykryta tylko wtedy, gdy ktoś świadomie porówna sumy.
2. **Manifest też jest lokalnym plikiem.** Nie ma podpisu, więc ktoś, kto zmienia dane celowo, może przy okazji podmienić sumy w manifeście. Chroni to więc przed przypadkowymi zmianami, a nie przed celowym fałszerstwem. Pewniejsze byłoby porównanie z sumami z niezależnego źródła, na przykład od prowadzącego, albo z sumą archiwum z `sources`, pobranego bezpośrednio od Apache.
3. **Zmiana bajtów to nie zawsze zmiana treści.** Na przykład zamiana końców linii z LF na CRLF (częsta na Windows przy kopiowaniu przez git) też zmieni sumę, choć tekst wiadomości jest ten sam. Suma mówi, że plik się różni, ale nie mówi co ani czy to coś ważnego.
4. **Zgodna suma nie oznacza poprawnych danych.** Potwierdza tylko, że plik jest taki sam jak w chwili przygotowania. Jeśli jakaś etykieta była błędna od początku, suma tego nie wykryje.

Dla Twojego uruchomienia `input_sha256` w raporcie zgadza się z manifestem. Znaczy to, że `data/exercise.csv` nie zmienił się od przygotowania 22.10.2026 albo że ktoś zmienił go razem z manifestem.

exercise-004,"Subject: [ILUG] Re: Problems with RAID1 on cobalt raq3

On Mon, Aug 19, 2002 at 03:08:16PM +0100, John P. Looney mentioned:
>  This is likely because to get it to boot, like the cobalt, I'm actually
> passing root=/dev/hda5 to the kernel, not /dev/md0. 

 Just to solve this...the reason I was booting the box with
root=/dev/hda5, not /dev/md0 was because /dev/md0 wasn't booting - it
would barf with 'can't find init'.

 It turns out that this is because I was populating md0 with tar. Which
seems to have 'issues' with crosslinked files - for instance, it was
trying to make a hard link of glibc.so to hda - and failing. It was only
as I did it again with a friend present, that he spotted the errors, and
queried them. We noticed that the hard linked files just didn't exist on
the new rootfs.

 When we duplicated the filesystems with dump instead of tar, it worked
fine, I was able to tell lilo to use root=/dev/md0 and everything worked.

 Woohoo.

Kate

# Data for the first run

## Field definitions

| CSV field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `message_id` | Identifier within this packet; links to `raw/<message_id>.eml`. |
| `text` | Decoded subject (`Subject:`), a blank line, and the full message body. |
| `label` | Source dataset label: `spam` or `ham` (legitimate email). |

The label is not produced by our script. Do not infer it from a single word: a legitimate email can contain an advertising footer. One CSV record can span multiple lines because the text retains its paragraph breaks.

## Sources and preparation

Source: [Apache SpamAssassin public corpus](https://spamassassin.apache.org/old/publiccorpus/), archives [20030228_easy_ham.tar.bz2](https://spamassassin.apache.org/old/publiccorpus/20030228_easy_ham.tar.bz2) and [20030228_spam.tar.bz2](https://spamassassin.apache.org/old/publiccorpus/20030228_spam.tar.bz2). Prepared on 2026-10-22. The data is included locally; students do not need to download it.

Short, single-part `text/plain` messages were selected for manual inspection. This is not a random or representative sample for training or evaluating a filter. `demo.csv` and `exercise.csv` contain different messages. This historical corpus does not represent present-day email.

Transformations:

1. The selected archive members were preserved byte for byte in `raw/`, with new filenames matching `message_id`. These are originals **from the published corpus**, whose publisher had already modified some addresses and hostnames.
2. Python's standard-library `email` parser read each message using `policy.default`. The subject, body transfer encoding, and declared character encoding were decoded (ASCII when no charset was declared). Line endings were normalized to LF. Bodies were not truncated; quotations and footers were retained.
3. The `text` field was assembled as `Subject: <subject>`, two newlines, and the body. Other headers remain in the original `.eml` file, but are not included in the CSV.
4. Labels came from the archive directory: `easy_ham` → `ham`, `spam` → `spam`. Local identifiers were assigned, and the CSV files were saved as UTF-8 with LF line endings.

`manifest.json` records archive URLs and SHA-256 hashes, selected archive members, their `.eml` paths, and hashes of the originals and CSV packets. It supports reproducing the selection and checking it against the same archives. Filenames, identifiers, and labels are not input features for the future model.

## Usage terms

According to the [corpus description](https://spamassassin.apache.org/old/publiccorpus/readme.html), copyright in the message texts remains with the original senders. The SpamAssassin software license is not a license for these messages. The publisher instructs users not to send them through a live email system. In this project, we read files as text; we do not send the messages or open their links.

"""Rebuild exercise.csv from raw .eml files (per data/README.md) and diff with current file."""
import csv, hashlib, io, json, sys
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path

data = Path(sys.argv[1])
manifest = json.loads((data / "manifest.json").read_text())
rows = []
for m in manifest["messages"]:
    if m["packet"] != "exercise.csv":
        continue
    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes((data / m["raw_file"]).read_bytes())
    body = msg.get_content().replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    rows.append((m["message_id"], f"Subject: {msg['subject']}\n\n{body}", m["label"]))

buf = io.StringIO()
w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
w.writerow(["message_id", "text", "label"])
w.writerows(rows)
rebuilt = buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
print("rebuilt size:", len(rebuilt), "sha:", hashlib.sha256(rebuilt).hexdigest())
print("manifest sha:", manifest["packets"]["exercise.csv"]["sha256"])

cur = (data / "exercise.csv").read_bytes()
print("current size:", len(cur))
import difflib
for line in difflib.unified_diff(rebuilt.decode().splitlines(True), cur.decode().splitlines(True), "rebuilt", "current", n=1):
    print(repr(line))
